response.rationale: The material evidence (T1) directly supports the actor='alpha-team', action='sighted', object='comet-q', and mechanism='transit-timing-method' components of the hypothesis, explicitly stating 'the first confirmed sighting of comet Q, tracked by the Alpha team using the transit-timing method'. Neither piece of evidence specifies the place='alpha-observatory' or pins the interval to exactly [1950,1950], but absence of explicit attestation for these details is not a contradiction per the review criteria—only a concrete conflict (e.g., the actor being attested elsewhere in a different time period, or the place being outside any tradition tied to the actor) would warrant rejection. No such conflict appears in the supplied evidence, and no refuting evidence was provided. Therefore, there is no basis to reject the hypothesis on contradiction grounds; the unspecified place/date details remain unverified extrapolations (model-prior/inference) rather than falsified claims.
